title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 14/27 — "In London"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 14. While the narrator lies hidden in Surrey, the story turns to his younger brother George, a medical student in London — and to the great city learning the news too slowly.

Saturday's papers carry only a brief report: Martians at Woking, dislodged by heavy guns. George goes to Waterloo to catch a train down and finds the boards dark — Woking, Windsor, Chertsey all stopped — a gun train rolling through the station, and the police clearing the platforms. On Westminster Bridge the first pink placards cry the news, and by nightfall the newsboys are shouting of fighting at Weybridge and the Black Smoke.

From his attic he watches London wake in the small hours: bells, hammering at doors, a closed carriage galloping past, the whole street of chimneys standing against a red dawn. The morning dispatch says it plainly — the Martians are moving on London, and there is no stopping them. George takes the money from his drawer and steps out into a city of six million people beginning to run.

Chapter XIV of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "In London", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
